description:
Scizor vs Heracross: The Cost of Giving Up Priority

A short matchup introduction, then every actual move in this fixed-seed tactical example. Planned teaching choices; accuracy, damage, effects, priority and fainting resolved by Pokemon Showdown 0.11.11, Generation 9 National Dex. No items, switching, Mega or Tera.

Scizor is Bug/Steel; Heracross is Bug/Fighting. Heracross is faster (206 vs 166), but Bullet Punch has +1 priority. Megahorn is resisted Bug STAB. Swords Dance doubles Scizor's physical Attack. Close Combat is neutral Fighting STAB against Bug/Steel: the two type modifiers cancel. Its Defense and Special Defense drops make later physical hits stronger. All actual attacks in this example are physical.

Important planned mistake: at 10 HP, Scizor selects ordinary-priority Close Combat instead of Bullet Punch. Faster Heracross executes Close Combat first; Scizor's chosen move never occurs. This is deliberately a teaching error, not perfect or recommended play. Heracross wins with 93/364 HP (25.55%). Both use Swarm; it does not boost these low-HP Fighting/Steel attacks.

Declared level-100 builds, 31 IVs in each stat:
Scizor: Swarm; Serious; EVs 252 HP, 252 DEF, 4 ATK; Bullet Punch, Close Combat, Knock Off, Swords Dance.
Heracross: Swarm; Serious; EVs 252 HP, 252 DEF, 4 ATK; Megahorn, Close Combat, Stone Edge, Swords Dance.
Fixed seed: [28084, 61280, 27307, 25239].

This is one conditional simulated example, not a universal ranking, aggregate win probability or canon anime outcome. Full-scene AI illustrations, camera moves, exact animated HP and local Kokoro narration. Bullet Punch uses a silver-glow pre-attack portrait because its contact illustration was unavailable.
